propositions: A ticket description write succeeded and read-back verified at 14,997 chars, then a subsequent read returned 10,582 chars (an older revision) with no error reported, and the silent rollback was only caught by further read-back verification.

Optimistic concurrency did not reject the losing write despite documented protection via ConcurrencyError/exit 10, allowing a write that was verified as successful to be silently discarded afterwards.

Ticket edits concurrent with in-flight plan-review sidecar events (REVIEW_RESULT with sidecar_emitted: true) may trigger store reconvergence that silently reverts the newer write to an older revision.
A write that will be discarded must fail loudly with ConcurrencyError/exit 10 rather than report success and revert afterwards.
The constraint against editing a ticket during its own review is undocumented and conflicts with the revise-then-review loop that the plan-review gate documentation describes for authors.
